Refuted. The sre governance agent (SRE-1) tested the claim: the gateway cannot count invalid UTF-8 toward the breaker, and the server's proto parse rejects the same bytes. Residual: the direct Register path counts it in no yuzu_register_* series and YuzuGatewayUpstreamEncodeErrors warns; that residual is INFO and is recorded as G15-FU-UTF8-COUNT. The exact command transcript is in the SRE-1 report and was relayed, not re-run, by the ledger writer.
refuted_by: SRE-1 ran gateway_pb:encode_msg on an agent id that is invalid UTF-8: the call raised badarg, which the gateway maps to {local_error,_}, so the circuit breaker is untouched. protoc --decode of the same bytes shows the server's own parse also rejects them. (Relayed from the sre agent's report; the verbatim command and output are not in the ledger input.)
refuted_by_reporter: sre governance agent (subagent of the authoring session; independence asserted, not enforced)
adjudicated_by: sre governance agent (SRE-1; subagent of the authoring session, not the change's author; independence asserted, not enforced). Separation applied: the de-escalation rule for a refuted reporter-HIGH finding.
adjudication_rationale: The reporter's HIGH rested on the claim that an invalid-UTF-8 id reaches the server and counts toward the gateway breaker. SRE-1's evidence is that gateway_pb:encode_msg raises badarg on the invalid bytes, which is mapped to {local_error,_} and does not touch the breaker, and that the server's proto parse rejects the same bytes. The claim is therefore false, not merely lower; the residual is an observability gap at INFO, kept as a deferred follow-up.

== Resource Ledger (C++) ==
No new fd/HANDLE/SOCKET/FILE*/sqlite3*/OpenSSL/BCrypt object, no allocated C string, no mapped library, no
subprocess, no thread, no callback context, no new temp path in production code. `PgPool` hunks only wrap
already-owned `PQerrorMessage` text (borrowed `const char*` copied into the token fn before the PGconn is
finished). Tests: test_pg_pool.cpp builds a salted (`unique_temp_path`, `yuzu_test_` prefix) NAME for a Unix-socket
directory that is never created, so no filesystem object exists; test_tag_store.cpp `exec_ddl` opens a raw libpq
connection (`PQconnectdb`) owned by a move-only `PgConn` RAII owner, released on REQUIRE unwind. (CORRECTED
2026-10-16 after CPS-1: an earlier version of this paragraph said pool tests create a TempDir and omitted
exec_ddl.) Shell
harness runs the agent as a child it kills in the failure branch (`kill -9`). No manual cleanup in new C++.

== Resource Ledger addendum (UP-8 fix commit ff34824ca and its tests; added after cpp-safety CPS8B-2) ==
Production, all move-only and released on every path: `PgPool::Lease` (one each in `AuthDB::add_pending` and `AuthDB::ensure_enrolled`, acquired by `try_acquire_for(kWriteTimeout)` and moved straight into `with_txn_on`), `PgTxn` inside `run_in_txn` (rolled back on every false return or exception), one `PgResult` per statement inside the callbacks. No fd, HANDLE, SOCKET, FILE*, OpenSSL object, C string, subprocess, callback context or production thread was added. Tests: a side `PgConn` (RAII) plus an open row-lock transaction on it (released by DELETE and COMMIT, or by the scope guard's ROLLBACK, or by `PQfinish`), one test-local `std::thread` (the race test worker) whose owner is `run_with_row_vanishing_before_write`; it is joined on every path including a throwing assertion (statuses are captured, joined, then asserted) and by a scope guard that rolls back the side connection first, and `count_scalar` owns a `PgConn` and `PgResult`. No `std::jthread` (Apple Clang lacks it).

== Resource Ledger addendum 2 (final-sweep fixes; added after cpp-safety SW-CPS-1) ==
Test side only, nothing new in production C++ for resource ownership:
- `read_server_source` (`tests/unit/server/test_agent_service_impl.cpp`): a block-scoped `std::ifstream`, RAII-closed at function exit, one file at a time, the open checked by `REQUIRE(in.is_open())` before the read.
- The `std::filesystem::recursive_directory_iterator` walk over `server/core/src` (about 809 files; the default options do not follow directory symlinks), holding one directory handle per level for the duration of the loop, released by the iterator's destructor.
- `yuzu::test::LogCapture`: swaps the global spdlog default logger and level for a capture sink (RAII; the previous logger and level are restored by `stop()` or the destructor, so a failing REQUIRE cannot leave the swap in place).
- `JoinOnExit` (scope guard in the vanishing-row race test): borrows a `std::thread&` and a `PGconn*`, owns neither; its destructor issues `ROLLBACK` on the side connection and joins the worker if still joinable, so the worker never outlives the connection or the test.
- The `static const std::regex` objects in the test helpers (`register_invalid_id_reasons`, `count_charset_flag_true`): function-local magic statics, constructed once, immutable, destroyed at process exit.
